fact: The backend of Auftrag #2 is the server service `ClaudeAccounts` in `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:140-155` with four methods: `remember({instanceId, name})`, `list`, `forget({name})` and `switch({instanceId, name})`. Nothing in `packages/contracts`, `packages/client-runtime`, `apps/web` or `apps/mobile` references it yet, and no WebSocket handler in `apps/server/src/ws.ts` calls it.

`ClaudeAccounts.layer` is already built into the production runtime as `layerClaudeAccountsProvided` (`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/runtimeLayer.ts:341-351`) and merged into `layerProduction` (`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/runtimeLayer.ts:396`), which reaches `Ws.layer` via `apps/server/src/server.ts:498-710`. A handler can `yield* ClaudeAccounts.ClaudeAccounts` without new wiring.

Account switching is Linux-only: every `ClaudeAccounts` method first runs `requireLinux`, failing with `ClaudeAccountError` reason `unavailable` when `HostProcess.Platform` is not `"linux"` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:253-257`). `HostProcess.Platform` is a `Context.Reference` defaulting to `process.platform`, so tests override it (`packages/shared/src/HostProcess.ts:7-9`).

`ClaudeAccountError` is a `Schema.TaggedError` with `reason` (17 literals: unavailable, setupNotFound, setupUnreadable, notLoggedIn, invalidName, nameInUse, alreadyRemembered, accountNotFound, storage, currentNotRemembered, needsFreshLogin, loginCheckFailed, switchFailed, switchRollbackFailed, externalClaudePrograms, processCheckFailed, sessionStopFailed), optional `instanceId` and optional `name`, and a computed `message` getter (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:45-112`). It lives in `apps/server`, so it must move to `packages/contracts` to appear in an Rpc error union.

`RememberedClaudeAccount {name, email}`, `ClaudeSetupAccountState {instanceId, displayName: string|null, active: {email, rememberedAs: string|null}|null}`, `ClaudeAccountList {accounts, setups}` and `ClaudeSwitchResult {instanceId, active, affectedInstanceIds}` are already `Schema.Struct`s in `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:114-138` and can move to contracts unchanged.

Several `ClaudeAccountError` messages name internal identifiers or CLI commands: `needsFreshLogin` and `switchRollbackFailed` tell the user to run `claude auth login` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:97, 103`), and setupNotFound, setupUnreadable, notLoggedIn, currentNotRemembered, switchFailed, externalClaudePrograms, processCheckFailed and sessionStopFailed interpolate the raw `${this.instanceId}` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:79-109`). Shown as-is, they break AK-31/AK-32.

The integration test pins the `needsFreshLogin` and `switchRollbackFailed` message strings (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts:1374, 2214`); changing those texts alters existing tests and needs a written justification in the hand-off.

`remember` reads the login of the named setup (`readClaudeSetupLogin(setup.paths)`), trims the name, refuses `invalidName` (1-64 chars, no control characters), `nameInUse` (case-insensitive `sameName`) and `alreadyRemembered` (same account identity), then saves under `accountsLock` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:343-386`).

`list` returns all remembered accounts globally (not per setup) plus one `ClaudeSetupAccountState` per Claude provider instance; one unreadable setup yields `active: null` instead of failing the list (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:388-423`).

`forget({name})` removes the remembered account under `accountsLock` and fails `accountNotFound` if missing; it never touches a setup's login files, so forgetting the active account keeps the setup logged in and `list` then shows `rememberedAs: null` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:425-438`).

`switch` runs entirely under `accountsLock` (`Semaphore.make(1)`), so a second concurrent switch call waits and then runs instead of being refused (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:251, 793-828`). Every refusal (`checkSwitch`) happens before anything is stopped, and a switch to the already-active account returns at once as `AlreadyActive` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:486-555, 802-803`).

`checkSwitch` refuses `currentNotRemembered` when the setup's logged-in account is not remembered, `accountNotFound` for an unknown target, `externalClaudePrograms` when unmarked Claude programs use the config dir, and `needsFreshLogin`/`loginCheckFailed` from `ClaudeLoginCheck` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:486-555`). The login check can take about 29 s (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:560`).

Before writing login files, `switch` interrupts the setup's running T3 turns with their queues held (`stopSetupSessions`, reason "Stopped for a Claude account switch"), waits up to `CLAUDE_SWITCH_STOP_TIMEOUT = 10 s`, then resumes held queues in an `ensuring` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:157-158, 719-767, 805-826`). A stopped turn is therefore not continued automatically, and a new message runs on the new login.

Server rule for "a turn is running on a setup": `activeRunsOn(affected)` walks `projections.getRecoveryThreadIds("runtime")` and `ThreadManagementService.latestActiveRun`, matching `run.providerInstanceId` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:618-631`). Active run statuses are preparing, starting, running, waiting (`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ThreadManagementService.ts:444-451`).

`sameConfigDirSetups` makes a switch affect every Claude instance on the same config dir; `ClaudeSwitchResult.affectedInstanceIds` lists them, requested one first (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:132-138`).

Remembered accounts, including OAuth tokens, are stored as one versioned JSON secret named `claude-accounts` in `ServerSecretStore` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:160, 314-341`). `ServerSecretStore` writes `${stateDir}/secrets/<name>.bin` with dir mode 0700 and files 0600, no encryption (`apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.ts:160-236`, `apps/server/src/config.ts:147`).

Tokens are held as `Redacted` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:183, 322`), errors never keep a cause that could quote a login ("No cause is kept", `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:311`; `apps/server/src/provider/claudeLoginFiles.ts:110`), and logs carry only operation, name, instanceId and outcome (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:385, 604-610`).

`ClaudeAccountError` on the wire carries only `reason`, optional `instanceId` and optional account `name`; no token, path or email is in it (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:66-72`). The `email` of remembered accounts does reach clients through `list` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts:114`).

`readClaudeSetupLogin(paths: ClaudeSetupPaths)` reads `${configDir}/.credentials.json` and `paths.accountConfigPath` and returns `Option<ClaudeSetupLogin>` (`apps/server/src/provider/claudeLoginFiles.ts:87-108`). It accepts any `{configDir, accountConfigPath}`, so it can read a throwaway dir, as `ClaudeLoginCheck` already does (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeLoginCheck.ts:102-105`).

`ClaudeSetupLogin` holds `claudeAiOauth: Redacted<JsonObject>`, `oauthAccount` and `identity {email, accountUuid, organizationUuid}` (`apps/server/src/provider/claudeLoginFiles.ts:15-27`); accounts are compared by accountUuid plus organizationUuid, not by email (`apps/server/src/provider/claudeLoginFiles.ts:39-40`).

`resolveClaudeSetupPaths(config, env)` returns `{configDir, accountConfigPath}`; `.claude.json` sits inside the config dir only when `homePath` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set, otherwise at `~/.claude.json` (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:30-49`). `resolveClaudeHomePath` checks `config.homePath`, then inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, then `~/.claude` (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:12-28`).

Every Claude CLI T3 spawns must use `makeClaudeEnvironment(config, baseEnv)`, which marks it with `T3CODE_CLAUDE_OWNER_PID` (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:56-65`); an unmarked Claude process on a setup's config dir blocks every switch (`docs/internals/providers.md:52-60`). `makeClaudeTerminalEnvironment` sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when `homePath` is set (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:71-91`).

`ClaudeLoginCheck.check` creates a throwaway dir with `fileSystem.makeTempDirectoryScoped({prefix: "t3-claude-login-check-"})`, writes login files at mode 0600, and removes the dir when the scope closes (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeLoginCheck.ts:78-133`). A crash before the scope closes leaves the dir in the OS temp dir; nothing sweeps it.

No code anywhere in `apps/server` or `packages` starts `claude auth login`; the command appears only in user-facing texts (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:647`, `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:136-145`). Whether its browser login can finish when the browser is on another device (pasted code vs localhost callback) is not verified in the repository.

The Claude driver has no `auth` controller: its `ProviderInstance` has `instanceId`, `snapshot`, `invalidateCaches`, `snapshotForCwd`, `orchestrationAdapter`, `textGeneration`, `consumeResetCredit` (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:385-408`), so `provider.auth.start` on a Claude instance fails with "This provider does not support sign-in in T3 Code." (`apps/server/src/provider/ProviderAuthService.ts:74-89`).

`ProviderAuthService.start` and `logout` run under `credentialChanges.withPermit` and pass `stopSessions`, which releases every live provider session on the instance with `reason: "manual_shutdown"` (`apps/server/src/provider/ProviderAuthService.ts:94-172, 228-270`). Routing add-account through `provider.auth.*` would therefore risk stopping turns.

The generic sign-in attempt tracker is `ProviderAuthFlow.make` in `packages/provider-core/src/server/providerAuthFlow.ts:60-90`: one attempt per controller, owner-checked (`requireFlow`, `:108-123`), default timeout `300_000` ms (`:77`), state only in memory in a `SubscriptionRef` (`:88`). `cancel` interrupts the flow fibers and publishes `phase: "cancelled"` (`:429-449`); interruption closes scoped resources.

Sign-in attempts do not survive a server restart: `ProviderAuthFlow` keeps them in memory only (`packages/provider-core/src/server/providerAuthFlow.ts:88-90`), and there is no disconnect-triggered cancel in it (no disconnect handling in the file). A client closing without cancelling leaves an attempt alive until its timeout.

The closest existing "run a login CLI in a PTY" pattern is the ACP registry terminal sign-in: `runTerminal` calls `pty.value.spawn({shell, args, cwd, cols: 80, rows: 24, env})`, streams output into `setInteraction({type: "terminal", output, outputOffset}, respond)`, kills the process in a finalizer and fails on non-zero exit (`packages/provider-acp-registry/src/server/auth.ts:158-228`). It obtains the PTY via `Effect.serviceOption(PtyAdapter.PtyAdapter)` (`packages/provider-acp-registry/src/server/auth.ts:43`).
A PTY adapter is provided server-wide: `layerPtyAdapter = NodePtyAdapter.layer` (`apps/server/src/server.ts:233`, provided at `apps/server/src/server.ts:629`).

`ProviderAuthState` has `phase` (idle, starting, waiting, verifying, succeeded, failed, cancelled), `flowId`, `authorizationUrl`, `expiresAt`, `message`, `methods`, `interaction`, `credentialOwner` (`packages/contracts/src/providerSetup.ts:118-140`). `ProviderAuthInteraction` includes `terminal {output <=16384, outputOffset?}` and `ProviderAuthResponse` includes `terminal {data <=4096, size?}` for keystrokes and resize (`packages/contracts/src/providerSetup.ts:44-92`).

Existing provider-auth RPCs: `provider.auth.start` (`ProviderAuthStartInput {instanceId, methodId?, returnUrl?, callbackMode?}`), `provider.auth.complete` (`{instanceId, flowId, callbackUrl}`), `provider.auth.cancel` (`{instanceId, flowId}`) and the stream `provider.auth.subscribe` (`packages/contracts/src/providerSetup.ts:102-153`, `packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:635-693`).

Codex ChatGPT sign-in does not run `codex login`; `makeCodexChatGptAuth` runs T3's own PKCE OAuth with a temporary `127.0.0.1` loopback listener in `Effect.acquireRelease` (`apps/server/src/provider/CodexChatGptAuth.ts:468-541`). For remote browsers the user pastes the final localhost URL, validated by `codexCallbackUrl` (`apps/server/src/provider/CodexChatGptAuth.ts:542-562`).

WebSocket RPC method names live in the single `WS_METHODS` object in `packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:380`, dotted `area.verb` or `area.sub.verb` (e.g. `providerAuthStart: "provider.auth.start"` at `:411`, `serverRefreshProviders: "server.refreshProviders"` at `:475`).

Each method is declared `const WsXxxRpc = Rpc.make(WS_METHODS.xxx, { payload, success, error, stream? })` using `effect/rpc/Rpc` (`packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:25, 635-639`), and must be listed in `WsRpcGroup = RpcGroup.make(...)` (`packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:1882`), which ends with `.middleware(RpcScopeAuthorization)` (`packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:2081`).

Rpc errors are `Schema.Union([DomainError, EnvironmentAuthorizationError])`; the provider-setup family shares `ProviderSetupRpcError` (`packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:627`). `ProviderSetupError` is a `Schema.TaggedError` whose `message` getter returns `detail` and whose doc says "Safe setup failure text. Never include OAuth codes, URLs, or native token data." (`packages/contracts/src/providerSetup.ts:187-200`).
Only a TaggedError's fields cross the wire; the client rebuilds `message` from its own copy of the class, so a `message` getter defined in `packages/contracts` gives web and desktop the same text.

`packages/contracts/src/index.ts` re-exports each domain file with `export * from "./<file>.ts"` (e.g. `providerSetup.ts`, `providerUsageLimits.ts` at `packages/contracts/src/index.ts:19-21`); a new contracts domain file is added the same way.

All WebSocket handlers are in `apps/server/src/ws.ts`: `layerWsRpc(currentSession, ...)` builds `ServerWsRpcGroup.toLayer(Effect.gen(...))` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1183-1190`) with `ServerWsRpcGroup = WsRpcGroup.middleware(RpcInstrumentation)` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:546`) and the handler map `ServerWsRpcGroup.of({...})` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1806`).

Services are pulled into the handler closure at the top of `layerWsRpc`, e.g. `const providerAuth = yield* ProviderAuthService.ProviderAuthService;` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1279`), `const providerRegistry = yield* ProviderRegistry.ProviderRegistry;` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1271`) and `providerInstances = yield* ProviderInstanceRegistry.ProviderInstanceRegistry` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1274`).

AGENTS.md: server features are services, and `ws.ts` handlers stay thin: decode, one service call, map errors (`AGENTS.md:154`). Existing handlers are one-line delegations such as `[WS_METHODS.providerAuthLogout]: (input) => providerAuth.logout(input)` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:2343-2358`); longer ones use `Effect.fnUntraced` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:2179-2181`).
Domain errors are mapped inline with `Effect.mapError` into the wire error type in handlers, e.g. driver errors become `ProviderSetupError` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:2236-2245, 2330-2339`).

`layerWsRpc` is built per WebSocket connection: after `serverAuth.authenticateWebSocketUpgrade(request)` the server calls `RpcServer.make(ServerWsRpcGroup, ...)` and provides `RpcAuthorization.layer(session.scopes, ...)` and `layerWsRpc(session, ...)` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:3164-3220`).

Every Rpc must have exactly one required scope in `RPC_REQUIRED_SCOPES ... satisfies Readonly<Record<WsRpcMethod, AuthEnvironmentScope>>` (`apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts:39-211`); a missing entry is a compile error, and `apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.test.ts:36-37` checks it.

Provider credential mutations require `AuthProvidersManageScope = "providers:manage"` (`packages/contracts/src/auth.ts:33`): `providerAuthStart`, `providerAuthLogout`, `providerAuthSubscribe` map to it (`apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts:63-77`). `serverRefreshProviders` needs only `AuthOrchestrationReadScope` (`apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts:61`).

The scope middleware rejects a call with `rpcAuthorizationError(requiredScope)` when the session lacks the scope (`apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts:276-287`); payload-dependent scopes go in `requiredScopesForRpcCall` (`apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts:248-269`).

`CLIENT_GUARDED_RPC_SCOPES` (`packages/contracts/src/clientRpcPermissions.ts:15-52`) lets clients hide or disable actions by scope; it is spread into the server map (`apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts:40`). AGENTS.md asks new guarded mutations to be listed there, with UI availability read from the command's `permissionAtom` (e.g. `apps/web/src/components/chat/ThreadAutomationsPanel.tsx:63`).

The `provider.auth.*` methods are not in `CLIENT_GUARDED_RPC_SCOPES`; pages gate them with `useEnvironmentScope(environmentId, AuthProvidersManageScope)` (`apps/web/src/state/session.ts:24`, `apps/web/src/components/settings/CodexSetupSection.tsx:178`).

The WebSocket is authenticated at upgrade with a one-time ticket via `sessions.verifyWebSocketToken`, MCP-audience tokens rejected (`apps/server/src/auth/EnvironmentAuth.ts:1237-1249`); each session carries `scopes` enforced per RPC.

`RpcInstrumentation` keeps a map `satisfies Record<WsRpcMethod, string>` with a span area per method, e.g. `[WS_METHODS.providerAuthStart]: "provider"` (`apps/server/src/observability/RpcInstrumentation.ts:36-47, 215`); a new method needs an entry or the build breaks.

RPC handler tests in `apps/server/src/ws.test.ts` build `layerWsRpc(...)` against `Layer.mock(Service)({})` entries such as `Layer.mock(ProviderAuthService.ProviderAuthService)({})` (`apps/server/src/ws.test.ts:483`) and drive it with `RpcServer.makeNoSerialization(RpcGroup.make(WsXxxRpc), ...)` (`apps/server/src/ws.test.ts:602-631`). Adding `yield* ClaudeAccounts` to `layerWsRpc` requires a mock entry there.

`ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts` uses `@effect/vitest` `it.layer(NodeServices.layer)("ClaudeAccounts", ...)` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts:834`), replaces `ClaudeLoginCheck` with a scripted `Layer.succeed` (`:540-556`), uses `testClaudeDriver`/`makeFakeClaude` (`:268, 436-442`) and a fake `/proc` via `ClaudeExternalProcesses.layerWith({procRoot})` (`:558-559, 648-660`).

The `ClaudeAccounts` test stack uses the real `ServerSecretStore.layer` over `ServerConfig.layerTest(process.cwd(), {prefix: "t3-claude-accounts-test-"})`, in-memory SQLite and `ServerSettingsService.layerTest({providerInstances})` (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts:458-515`), pins `HostProcess.Platform`, `HomeDirectory` (temp), `Environment: {}` and `ProcessId: 4242` (`:665-682`), and asserts no token leaks into output (`assertNoLogin`, `:684-686`).

Guard rails: tests are red first, Chicago School, doubles only at real boundaries (provider CLIs, network, clock, filesystem outside a temp dir); no sleeps or polling; run one file with `node .loop-forge/test-scoped.mjs <path>` (`.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:31-50`). There is no e2e suite: each Gherkin criterion maps to a server integration test through the service or RPC boundary a client would use, and a criterion only a real client can prove is named unproven (`.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:52-56`).

Guard rails forbid touching any real Claude config dir (`~/.claude*`), even to read credentials; credential code is exercised only against temp dirs the test creates and removes (`.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:13-15`). No dev servers, browsers or computer use (`.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:17`).

Guard rails: contracts first, anything crossing the wire is typed in `packages/contracts`, and a change there must name every consumer updated (`.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:87-88`). Never edit `.loop-forge/` or `.github/`; a new dependency or external service stops with `Human` (`.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:92-94`).

Every ticket but the last is gated by `test-scoped.mjs` over the Auftrag's added or changed test files; the last ticket runs `test-affected.mjs`, which typechecks and runs suites of every affected package, `apps/server` taking over ten minutes (`.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:68-78`).
Changes must stay upstreamable to `pingdotgg/t3code`: no fork-only conventions in product code (`.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:7-9`).

AGENTS.md asks every feature to hit every surface: entry points, clients (web/desktop/mobile), contracts, reverse states (an added account needs a way out and a way to see it), connection modes, and docs (`AGENTS.md:65-76`). The Auftrag explicitly excludes the mobile app.

AGENTS.md forbids continuously repainting animations and "lying spinners" and asks for small WebSocket payloads (`AGENTS.md:17, 164`). The design store says the switch-in-progress indicator is static.
